siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Glacier, drive SR 542 east about 24 miles to the end of the highway at the large Artist Point parking lot.

siblingApproaches.approach: From the Artist Point trailhead (elev. ~5,100 ft, at the end of Mt. Baker Highway/SR 542, GPS approx. 48.847, -121.693) walk to the northwest corner of the large paved parking lot — the signed Table Mountain Trail #681 starts opposite the vault toilets, on the side of the lot away from the highway. The trail begins as a rock-lined gravel path that climbs gently before reaching its first switchback within a few hundred feet. From there the route ascends a tight set of rocky switchbacks blasted directly into the cliff band on Table Mountain's southeast face — this is the crux of the approach: a

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Glacier, drive SR 542 east about 24 miles to the end of the highway at the large Artist Point parking lot.

Baker Highway/SR 542, GPS approx. 48.847, -121.693) walk to the northwest corner of the large paved parking lot — the signed Table Mountain Trail #681 starts opposite the vault toilets, on the side of the lot away from the highway. siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: Start at the Twin Lakes trailhead (~5,200 ft), the rough, rutted end of Twin Lakes Road (many parties park short and walk the final rutted miles, as the road note indicates).

siblingApproaches.approach: Start at the Twin Lakes trailhead (~5,200 ft), the rough, rutted end of Twin Lakes Road (many parties park short and walk the final rutted miles, as the road note indicates). From the parking area pick up the signed High Pass Trail; at about a quarter mile it splits from the short spur up Winchester Mountain Lookout — stay left/north on the High Pass Trail. The trail contours along the west side of Winchester Mountain, dips across an unnamed minor saddle often called Low Pass (open views west to Tomyhoi Peak), then climbs steadily to High Pass itself (~5,960 ft, roughly 2 miles and about 750 f

siblingTrailheads.trailhead: Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road)
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From I-90 exit 34 near North Bend, follow 468th to Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road, turn right and drive 12 miles, passing the large Middle Fork parking area on the right. Cross the large concrete bridge, immediately turn right onto the gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap, and follow it about 6 miles to the gate and trailhead.

siblingApproaches.approach: Start at the Dingford Creek Trailhead gate and walk (or mountain-bike) the closed Middle Fork Snoqualmie River Road about 7 miles to the boot path for Hardscrabble Lakes, which starts roughly half a mile short of the old Hardscrabble Horse Camp, across the road from a large fallen log. Follow the climbers path east through forest to upper Hardscrabble Lake, staying near the inlet — straying left leads into cliff bands.

Drive to the Dingford Creek Trailhead gate via Middle Fork Snoqualmie River Rd / FSR 56 (about 18 mi from North Bend; the last several miles are rough gravel, high-clearance recommended). Hike the Dingford Creek Trail roughly 3.2 mi to the Hester Lake Trail junction, continue left (east) toward Myrtle Lake (about 2 more miles). From Myrtle Lake, leave the trail and climb steep, increasingly brushy terrain toward Big Snow Lake, then traverse right around Snowflake Lake before ascending gullies/a snow couloir on the mountain's NW flank to the upper rock fields.

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From I-90 exit 85 take SR-970 east 7 miles, turn left onto Teanaway Road, and after 7.1 miles bear right onto North Fork Teanaway Road. Where the pavement ends after 5.9 miles take the right fork onto FR-9737 and continue about 9.5 miles, keeping left at the Beverly Campground fork and right at the fork for the trailhead, to the parking area.

siblingApproaches.approach: From the Esmeralda Basin/Ingalls Lake Trailhead (end of Teanaway River Road/USFS Rd 9737), take the Ingalls Way Trail (#1390). At about 0.4 mile bear right at the junction onto Ingalls Way (Esmeralda Basin Trail #1394 continues straight); at roughly 1.4 miles pass the Longs Pass junction. The trail climbs steadily through forest and open slopes to Ingalls Pass (~6,500 ft) at about 3.0-3.1 miles, the Alpine Lakes Wilderness boundary and your first full view of Mount Stuart and the Ingalls group. From the pass, drop slightly and traverse climbers'-left across open slabs and talus (a boot path br

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive east on Paradise Road about 14 miles; the signed Narada Falls parking lot is on the right, about 1 mile before the Paradise area.

siblingTrailheads.trailhead: Pinnacle Saddle Trailhead (Reflection Lakes, Stevens Canyon Road)
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive Paradise Road about 15 miles to the Stevens Canyon Road junction, turn right and go 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking area.

From the Narada Falls parking lot on the road to Paradise, plowed year-round, climb the steep hillside about 200 ft to Stevens Canyon Road; when that road is open, roughly late May to mid-October, most parties park at the Reflection Lake pullout instead and skip the climb

siblingApproaches.approach: Begin at the Narada Falls parking area; travel via snowshoe/ski along the (closed, in winter) Reflection Lakes road, then traverse steep hillsides under Denman Peak toward Lane Peak's base, turning sharply uphill at the first steep avalanche funnel to reach the base of the couloir.

Same trailhead as the Classic Route: park at the Reflection Lake pullout on Stevens Canyon Road when it's open, or at the Narada Falls pullout in winter/spring when the road is snow-gated (a short, steep ~200 ft climb from Narada Falls regains the road). Walk the road about half a mile to the 90-degree bend, then drop south through open forest toward Tatoosh Creek (~4,500 ft), as with the Classic Route. Rather than climbing right toward the south-face saddle, stay low and work into the basin directly below Lane Peak's north face — the Zipper is the obvious left-leaning couloir splitting the ce

siblingTrailheads.trailhead: Dingford Creek / Middle Fork Snoqualmie Trailhead
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From I-90 near North Bend, take exit 34, turn left onto 468th Street and follow it to Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road. Go 12 miles to the large Middle Fork parking area, pass it, and turn right onto a gravel road just after the large concrete bridge, signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap. Follow it 6 miles over potholes to a gate, with the trailhead just past it.

siblingApproaches.approach: From the Dingford Creek Trailhead, where FR 56 is gated, follow Dutch Miller Gap Trail 1030 — the first 7.7 miles on the closed road to Hardscrabble Horse Camp — up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley toward Dutch Miller Gap, but do not go to the gap: leave the main Middle Fork Snoqualmie trail at a small steel bridge well before Dutch Miller Gap and cut cross-country south into Summit Chief Valley; the Northwest Face is visible on the east side of that valley — a distinctly different final leg than the Northeast Face's direct ridge approach.

From the Dutch Miller Gap Trailhead (the Dingford Creek Trailhead, where the road is gated), follow Dutch Miller Gap Trail 1030 up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley about 14-15 miles to Dutch Miller Gap, passing Hardscrabble Horse Camp and the Williams Lake trail junction along the way. Little Big Chief sits immediately southwest of the gap, reached from the gap itself by an off-trail scramble up the peak's east slope/northeast ridge, with a short but exposed class 4 notch as the crux below the summit. An alternate, longer approach comes from the east via the Necklace Valley Trail off Foss Riv

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Newhalem, drive SR-20 east about 14 miles; the trailhead parking is on the right between mileposts 134 and 135.

siblingApproaches.approach: The trip starts at the Ross Dam Trailhead on SR 20 (North Cascades Highway, ~2,050ft), where parking is right off the highway. From there it's about a 0.8-mile hike down the Ross Dam Trail to Ross Lake, then a boat shuttle (Ross Lake Resort water taxi, or a paddled canoe/packraft for parties without a shuttle reservation) roughly 9 miles up-lake to the Big Beaver Trailhead (~1,600ft) near the Big Beaver / 39 Mile camp area — this lake crossing is a key logistical step, not an afterthought, since Ross Lake Resort's shuttle season and hours govern when you can actually reach the trailhead. From

siblingTrailheads.trailhead: Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Marblemount, go straight past the last gas station onto Cascade River Road, cross the bridge and drive to the Eldorado Creek trailhead at mile 20, on the right; the last 10 miles are gravel.

siblingApproaches.approach: Start at the Eldorado Creek trailhead on Cascade River Road, follow the climbers' trail up Eldorado Creek into the Roush Creek basin, camp near the base of the East Ridge (about 7,500 ft), then cross the Inspiration and McAllister glaciers to Dorado Needle Col and make a loose fourth-class downclimb into the Marble Creek cirque, traversing to the toe of the arete near 6,000 ft. Typically a 3-day trip (approach day, climb day, exit day); the first roughly 800 ft of climbing is Class 4 before harder 5th-class sections.

Same as the East Ridge: Eldorado Creek trailhead (2,100 ft) via Cascade River Road, boulder field, Eldorado Creek basin, and the Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier to around 7,500-8,200 ft, where the Northeast Face angles off climbers' right of the standard glacier track.

name: E Ridge via Mesahchie Icefall Couloir variation

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east about 45 miles and turn right between mileposts 151 and 152 onto the signed Easy Pass road, which leads to the trailhead lot.

siblingApproaches.approach: Start at the Easy Pass/Fisher Creek Trailhead on SR-20 (marked pullout near milepost 151, about 5 miles west of Rainy Pass, elevation ~3,700 ft; room for roughly 10 cars, pit toilet, no water at the lot). Follow the Easy Pass Trail, which climbs steadily through forest and then open meadows/talus, gaining roughly 2,800 ft over about 3.6 miles to Easy Pass (~6,500 ft); budget 1.5-2 hours at a good pace. There are reliable streams along the lower trail but none right at the pass, so top off water before cresting. Do not descend into Fisher Creek: leave the trail just west of the pass, before it

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground, pass the campground and continue just under 4.5 miles to the trailhead.
usedBy: North Face of the Northwest Ridge

siblingTrailheads.trailhead: Bird Creek Meadows (Yakama Nation, Mirror Lake road)
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From the gas station in Trout Lake, take the right fork north and follow the Mount Adams Recreation Area signs on the main road, which becomes Road 82, about 14.7 miles, past Mirror Lake; just past it take the left fork to the Bird Lake trailhead. The Yakama Nation closed the recreation area by order in August 2026 because of nearby fires, and it is open only part of the year, so confirm it is open before you go.

From Trout Lake, drive north on Mount Adams Road to the V intersection with Forest Road 23, veer right and go about 1 mile, then turn left onto Forest Road 80 (signed South Climb) and follow it to its end. Turn right onto Forest Road 8040 and drive north past Morrison Creek Campground to the trailhead; the last 3 miles are very rough and narrow.
North from Trout Lake via Mt. Adams Road, Forest Road 80 and Forest Road 8040
From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground. Go past the campground and continue just under 4.5 miles to the trailhead at the road's end.
From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground, pass the campground and continue just under 4.5 miles to the trailhead.
From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to the junction with FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground. Follow FR-2329 past the campground for about 4.5 miles to the trailhead.

From Trout Lake, drive Mount Adams Road north to the V intersection with FR-23, veer right and go about 1 mile, then turn left onto FR-80 (signed South Climb) and follow it to its end. Turn right onto FR-8040 and drive north past Morrison Creek Campground to the old Cold Springs Camp; the last 3 miles are very rough and narrow.
From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to the junction with FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground. Follow FR-2329 past the campground for about 4.5 miles to the trailhead.

siblingApproaches.approach: From the Killen Creek Trailhead (FS Rd 2329, ~3 miles from Takhlakh Lake), follow Killen Creek Trail #113 through open, dusty lodgepole forest. Around 2.5 miles in you cross East Fork Adams Creek and its meadows (last reliable easy water before the high basin), then the trees thin as the trail climbs rockier terrain to meet the PCT (Trail #2000) at roughly 6,100 ft, about 3.1 miles from the trailhead. Continue straight across the PCT onto the High Camp Trail #10 for about 1.0 mile to High Camp / Adams Glacier Meadows at the edge of the Adams Glacier moraine (~6,900 ft) — a common base camp. Fr

Start at the Killen Creek trailhead on FR 2329 north of Takhlakh Lake and follow Killen Creek Trail 113 south for about 3.2 miles through lodgepole forest and meadows to the Pacific Crest Trail junction near 6,100 ft. Cross the PCT onto the High Camp Trail, a rocky boot path that climbs a volcanic spur for about a mile to High Camp on a flat bench near 6,900 ft; the whole carry is roughly four miles and 2,300 ft. Camp here, since water comes only from snowmelt and the site is very exposed to wind. Above camp the trail ends and the way crosses moraines and old lava flows toward the north side o

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From the Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead (~3,100 ft), at the end of Alpental Road off I-90 Exit 52

siblingApproaches.approach: Trailhead: Alpental Ski Area day-use lot at the end of Alpental Road, reached via I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass) — go north on Alpental Rd about 1.3 miles to the upper lot (~3,100 ft), the same trailhead used for Snow Lake, Denny Creek and Source Lake. Follow Snow Lake Trail #1013 about 3 miles (steady climbing through forest and brush) to Snow Lake at about 4,000 ft. Continue on the High Lakes Trail #1012 along the east shore and around the lake's north end roughly 2 more miles to Gem Lake, then pick up the unmaintained boot path on Gem Lake's west side that gains the ridge toward Roosevelt.

Where the pavement ends after 5.9 miles take the right fork onto FR-9737 and continue about 9.5 miles, keeping left at the Beverly Campground fork and right at the fork for the trailhead, to the parking area.

From I-90 Exit 85 near Cle Elum, cross the overpass and turn right onto SR-970, go 7 miles and turn left onto Teanaway Road. After 7.1 miles bear right onto North Fork Teanaway Road; where the pavement ends after 5.9 miles take the right fork onto FR-9737. Go 1.1 miles and stay left at the Beverly Campground fork, continue 6.7 miles and stay right at the fork signed for trail 1394, then drive 1.7 miles to the trailhead.

siblingTrailheads.trailhead: Esmeralda Basin Trailhead (North Fork Teanaway Rd)
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Cle Elum, take I-90 exit 85 and drive SR-970 east about 7 miles, then turn left onto Teanaway Road. Bear right as it becomes North Fork Teanaway Road, stay right at the fork signed for trail 1394, and drive about 1.7 more miles to the trailhead.

siblingApproaches.approach: From the Lake Stuart Trailhead, hike the Lake Stuart-Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599); at about 2.2 miles a fork splits toward Colchuck Lake (left) and Lake Stuart (right) — leave the maintained trail near the meadow around 4,500 ft and head southwest, following the south fork of Mountaineer Creek upstream. After a couple of miles, climb a steep talus/boulder slope into the hanging valley beneath Sherpa Peak and the Sherpa/Stuart Glaciers. Sherpa Glacier climbers ascend directly from this basin; Stuart Glacier Couloir climbers continue up into the couloir on Stuart's north side from the same basin.

From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (end of Eightmile Road/FR 7601, off Icicle Road/FR 7600), follow the Mountaineer Creek climbers' path past the Colchuck Lake turnoff toward the basins below the north side of the mountain, then work up into the Stuart Glacier basin beneath the col shared with the West Ridge.

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From the Nooksack Cirque Trailhead at the end of FR-34 off Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32)

siblingApproaches.approach: Approach is similar to the Beckey route via Ruth Creek and Price Lake moraine, but instead of ascending toward Price Glacier, traverse to the East Nooksack Glacier. Climb to the base of the south face (elevation approximately 6,500-7,000 feet), which rises directly above the glacier. Multiple variations exist depending on snow/ice conditions; the climb starts on the right side of the face.

From Bellingham, exit Interstate 5 at Sunset Drive/Mount Baker exit. Drive Mount Baker Highway (Washington 542) east through the town of Glacier (last resupply for groceries) and continue 13 miles to the Nooksack River bridge. Immediately before the bridge, turn left on Hannegan Pass Road (USFS #32). Stay left at 0.5 miles, then bear right onto Nooksack Cirque Road (#34) at about 1.4 miles from highway. Continue to the washout at 2.3 miles from the highway and park at Ruth Creek (elevation 2,156 feet). Hike the abandoned road beyond the washout for two miles to the original Nooksack Cirque tra

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From SR 20 at Marblemount, follow Cascade River Road about 23 miles to its end at the Cascade Pass parking lot. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is gravel.

siblingApproaches.approach: Drive Cascade River Road east from Marblemount roughly 23 miles (paved for about the first 10, then good gravel) to its end at the Cascade Pass Trailhead (3,660 ft; parking area and vault toilet, North Cascades NP wilderness permit required for overnight camps). In some seasons, including 2026, the road is gated to vehicles at Eldorado (mile 20), leaving the last 3 miles to the trailhead on foot or bike. From the trailhead, follow the Cascade Pass Trail, which switchbacks about 30 times up a forested rib, gaining roughly 1,400 ft in the first 2 miles before the grade eases into a long ascendin

siblingTrailheads.trailhead: Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road)
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From I-90 exit 34 near North Bend, follow 468th to Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road, turn right and drive 12 miles, passing the large Middle Fork parking area on the right. Cross the large concrete bridge, immediately turn right onto the gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap, and follow it about 6 miles to the gate and trailhead.

siblingApproaches.approach: From the Dingford Creek Trailhead (end of FR 56, Middle Fork Snoqualmie River Road), the fastest approach uses the gated continuation of the road as a mountain-bike/hike-in: roughly 7-8 miles of old roadbed (NF-5620) to Hardscrabble Horse Camp near the old Dutch Miller Gap Trailhead, saving significant time over walking it. From there, follow the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River / Dutch Miller Gap Trail (Trail 1030) east along the north bank of the river for several more miles — the tread here is in reasonable shape with minimal blowdown, passing dispersed camps and, in season, overgrown thimblebe

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (end of FR-7601 off Icicle Creek Road)

From Leavenworth, drive US-2 west 0.8 mile, turn left onto Icicle Road for about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR-7600), stay right onto FR-7601 and follow it about 4 miles to the trailhead. The last stretch closes in winter, typically November to May.

From Leavenworth, drive US-2 to the western edge of town and turn onto Icicle Road; after about 8.5 miles turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR-7600), stay right onto FR-7601 and follow it about 4 miles to the trailhead. FR-7601 closes to vehicles every winter, typically November to May.

siblingApproaches.approach: Standard access is via Aasgard Pass into the Core Enchantments: Stuart Lake Trailhead → Stuart Lake Trail (2.5 mi) → Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A, crossing Mountaineer Creek and switchbacking up to Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft, ~4.1 mi/2,000 ft). From the south-end boulder field, climb Aasgard Pass (1.25 mi, ~2,000 ft of steep, loose scree/dirt — the crux of the approach, hazardous under lingering snow into early July with a hidden creek/moat beneath the talus, and avalanche-prone in shoulder season). From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (3,400 ft) at the end of FS Road 7601, follow the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the signed Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599A) junction. Turn left, cross Mountaineer Creek (a rock-hop/log crossing and the last reliable, easy water source for a while), and switchback up 1.6 miles through forest to Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft) — roughly 4.1 miles and 2,000 ft from the car. Boulder-hop along the lake's east shore to the boulder field at its south end (about 5.5 miles in, 2,500 ft gained), then pick up the climbers' trail/talus leading to the base of Aasgard Pass. From I-90 exit 85 take SR-970 east 7 miles, turn left onto Teanaway Road, and after 7.1 miles bear right onto North Fork Teanaway Road. Where the pavement ends after 5.9 miles take the right fork onto FR-9737 and continue about 9.5 miles, keeping left at the Beverly Campground fork and right at the fork for the trailhead, to the parking area.

siblingApproaches.approach: The North Ridge is most commonly approached from the north via the Stuart Lake Trailhead (reached by Icicle Creek Road/Eightmile Creek Road out of Leavenworth). Follow the Stuart Lake Trail (#1599) along Mountaineer Creek roughly 3.5-4 miles, climbing gently through forest. Before reaching Stuart/Colchuck Lake, leave the maintained trail, cross Mountaineer Creek, and pick up a boot path/cairned route that climbs talus benches on the slope west of the creek, staying a couple hundred feet above the trees before dropping back toward the creek, aiming for the Argonaut-Sherpa basin. From the Esmeralda Basin/Longs Pass Trailhead (end of Teanaway River Road/FS-9737, ~4,300 ft), take the Longs Pass Trail (#1229) roughly 2.3 miles and about 2,300 ft of gain to Longs Pass (~6,200 ft), a broad open saddle. From the pass, drop steeply down the north side (a boot path, with snow fingers usable for glissading in early season) about 1,300-1,400 ft to the Ingalls Creek drainage (~4,800 ft). Ford or rock-hop Ingalls Creek (can run high with early-season snowmelt) and pick up the Ingalls Creek Trail, following it right (east) about a half to full mile to the Beverly-Turnpike Trail jun

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From the drivable end of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (NF-56)
Start at the Pete Lake Trailhead (~2,840 ft) at the end of Cooper Lake Road (Forest Road 46) off the Salmon La Sac Road.

siblingApproaches.approach: Approach from the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley (North Bend side): drive the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (NF-56) to its plowed/drivable end, then bike or hike the remaining distance (about 1 mile in the FA party's case) into the valley. Continue on foot through snowy forest along the valley trail, crossing multiple braids of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River (the crux of the approach in high water), then climb to a camp below the north face. The FA party's full approach from vehicle to camp took about 6.5 hours.

Start at the Pete Lake Trailhead (~2,840 ft) at the end of Cooper Lake Road (Forest Road 46) off the Salmon La Sac Road. Follow the Pete Lake Trail (#1323) roughly 4.5 miles of gentle, mostly flat forest walking along the Cooper River to Pete Lake. From Pete Lake, continue up the Lemah Creek/Lemah Meadows drainage (watch for windfall and thick vine maple in the meadow bypass) to join the Pacific Crest Trail; turn right (north) and climb the PCT's long switchback section roughly 4-4.5 more miles to Lower and Upper Vista Lake (~5,500-5,600 ft) — camp is commonly made here, making this a two-day

siblingTrailheads.trailhead: Goodell Creek / Upper Goodell Group Camp trailhead (SR-20, Newhalem)
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Burlington drive about 60 miles east on SR-20 to milepost 119 near Newhalem, where the steep, narrow dirt access road to the Upper Goodell group campground leaves the highway.

siblingApproaches.approach: From the Goodell Creek trailhead (~600 ft elevation, an unsigned pullout on an unpaved spur road off SR-20 directly across from Newhalem/Goodell Creek Campground), the climbers' trail parallels Goodell Creek for an easier 4.5 miles before a punishing 2.5-mile, ~4,700 ft push to treeline in Terror Basin (total ~7 mi / ~5,200 ft gain to camp) -- the tread is faint even when snow-free, brush is dense, and there are Class 3 root-pull sections through cliff bands. Most parties reach Terror Basin in one long day of roughly 6-7 hours. From Terror Basin, cross 'The Barrier' -- the basin's steep west h

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Cle Elum, drive SR-903 north about 17 miles past Lake Cle Elum and turn left onto Road 4600 (Cooper Lake Road). Drive Road 4600 about 7 miles over Cooper Pass, then stay on Road 4600 about 3 more miles down to the trailhead.

siblingApproaches.approach: Trailhead: Mineral Creek Trailhead (Trail #1331), roughly 2,360-2,400 ft, reached via FR-4600 over Cooper Pass. From the parking area the trail promptly crosses the Kachess River — look for logs spanning it; when they're not in place it's a short, easy wade. The trail then climbs gently north through second-growth and brushy old avalanche paths, muddy in spots with the occasional blowdown to step over. siblingApproaches.route: Middle Peak via South Face - South Chimney
siblingApproaches.approach: Same trailhead and initial trail as the East/Main Peak standard route: Mineral Creek Trailhead (2,400 ft), across the Kachess River ford, 1.7 miles of trail to the Mineral Creek crossing, then about 1 mile through vine maple brush to the base of the south-side talus slope below Middle Peak.

siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (end of FR-7601 off Icicle Creek Road, ~3,400 ft)

siblingApproaches.approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (~3,400 ft, reached via ~8.7 mi of Icicle Creek Road southwest of Leavenworth), follow the Stuart Lake Trail south along Mountaineer Creek. At about 2.5 miles, bear left (south) at the signed junction onto the Colchuck Lake Trail (this junction is also where the Lake Stuart fork continues straight); the trail crosses Mountaineer Creek on a log/boulder crossing that can be a wet, awkward ford in early season high water. Continue climbing through forest and over a boulder field to Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft) at roughly 4.3 miles from the trailhead — this is the last r

From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (Mountaineer Creek Trail #1599, elev. ~3,400 ft; Northwest Forest Pass required) at the end of Icicle Creek/Eightmile Road (FR 7601), follow the trail steadily uphill through forest along Mountaineer Creek. At about 2.5 miles, bear left at the signed junction onto the Colchuck Lake Trail (the right fork continues to Lake Stuart). Continue climbing, crossing a boulder-strewn section near the outlet, to reach Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft) at roughly mile 4, having gained about 2,000-2,100 ft — this is the last reliable water source before Aasgard Pass.
